stem: At Larkspur Group, retail and wholesale each have a project with its own team permissions. The shared `pricing` workspace must be usable by both teams through permissions. The Default Project also holds other teams' workspaces, and neither team should end up able to open workspaces it does not already use. What is the correct approach?

choices.text: Add the `pricing` workspace to both projects at the same time
Scope a variable set to both projects to make the `pricing` workspace join each
Keep `pricing` in one project and grant the other team access on the workspace itself
Move `pricing` into the Default Project and rely on that project's permissions

rationale: Every workspace belongs to exactly one project, and permissions can be set at project and workspace scope, so the second team can be granted access directly on the workspace. Placing a workspace in two projects is not possible. A variable set scoped to a project applies variables to the workspaces already in it and does not change which project a workspace belongs to. Moving the workspace into the Default Project either leaves both teams without access, because each project has a separate permissions set, or, if both teams are granted access there, gives them the other workspaces that start in the Default Project.
